an.help:
Analysis of a family tree stored in the investigation database (SQLite).

Usage: python analyse_arbre.py <db> <command> [options]

Commands (English aliases in brackets)
  stats                      coverage: dates, places, sources, level of certainty
  tache [--racine X] [--type T]  (task) propose the task of the day (changes daily, skips what is already in research_log);
                             T = preuve | remonter | valider | manquant | correlation | parente
                             (aliases: proof | climb | validate | missing | correlation | kinship)
  frontiere [--racine X]     (frontier) ancestors with no known parents, ranked by how easy they are to research
  anomalies                  inconsistencies to check (impossible dates, implausible ages)
  manquants [--racine X]     (missing) absent parent, unusual gaps between siblings, unknown deaths
  correlations               occupations and places: who, where, when
  parente A B                (kinship) kinship and estimated genetic closeness between two people
  trouver PATTERN            (find) look a person up by name (returns the identifier)

X, A, B: numeric identifier from the database or part of a name ("Mary SMITH"). Standard library only.
an.stats.empty: The database is empty. Import a tree (`gedcom_import.py`) or add people, then run again.
an.stats.dates: With a birth year: {b} ({bp}%); with a death year: {d} ({dp}%)
an.stats.hint: → As long as everything is level B, nothing is proved by a record: see `tache`.
an.frontier.title: Ancestors with no known parents: {n} (easiest to research first)
an.anom.born_after_mother: born {gap} years after his or her mother {name} (no. {pid})
an.anom.born_after_father: born {gap} years after his or her father {name} (no. {pid})
an.anom.born_after_death: born in {b}, after the death ({pd}) of {name} (no. {pid})
an.anom.title: {n} inconsistencies to check (the source may be wrong, or the date misread)
an.miss.gap: gap of {gap} years between {n1} ({y1}) and {n2} ({y2}): missing child?
an.miss.title: {n} leads on missing people or information
an.corr.places: Birth regions (second part of the place name):
an.corr.trades: Most frequent occupations, with the family names and regions involved:
an.corr.inherit: Same occupation as a parent: {same} cases out of {total} ({pct}%)
an.deg.uncle_n: {up} generation(s) above the aunt/uncle level (common ancestor {m} generations up)
an.kin.nocommon: No common ancestor found between {a} and {b} in this tree.
an.kin.nocommon2: (No common ancestor in the tree does not mean no link: branches stop at the known frontier.)
an.kin.head: {a}  ↔  {b}
an.kin.row: common ancestor: {x} — {n1} gen. from A, {n2} gen. from B ({paths} path(s)) → {degree}
an.kin.result: Estimated genetic closeness (Wright's coefficient of relationship): {r:.4f} ≈ {pct:.2f}% of DNA shared on average
an.kin.floor: Estimate from the known tree, ignoring inbreeding of ancestors: a minimum value.
an.task.title: Task of the day — {date}
an.task.end: At the end: log the search (even if it finds nothing) in research_log, and the facts found in evidence with their level.
an.task.nothing: Nothing new in this category today; try `frontiere`, `anomalies` or `manquants`.
an.task.proof.title: Prove a birth
an.task.proof.why: {person}: the tree gives the birth in {year} ({place}), level B.
an.task.proof.how: Departmental archives, civil registers of the place: read the record, note marginal remarks, parents and witnesses. Aim for level A.
an.task.climb.title: Go back one generation
an.task.climb.how: Look for the birth or baptism record, then the parents' marriage record (often in the bride's place). Geneanet: name index + registers.
an.task.validate.title: Check a suspicious entry
an.task.validate.how: Find the record or the cited source; decide between a typing error, a namesake and a misread date.
an.task.missing.title: Find a missing person or piece of information
an.task.missing.how: Birth records of the couple's children, censuses, ten-year death tables.
an.task.correlation.title: Explore a correlation
an.task.correlation.why: Run `correlations`: occupations, areas and migrations of the family.
an.task.correlation.how: Pick an occupation or an area that recurs, then look for trade or local archives.
an.task.kinship.title: Measure a kinship
an.task.kinship.why: Two people named {surname}: {a} and {b}. Are they related? `parente {ia} {ib}`.
an.task.kinship.how: If no common ancestor appears, that is a lead: look for the link in the records (marriages, witnesses) or note a possible namesake.
dev.help:
Simplified legal devolution (French law, Civil Code art. 731 ff.) from the local tree.

Usage: python devolution.py <db> <deceased> [--deces YEAR] [--tous] [--md file.md]

  <deceased>    identifier from the database or part of the name
  --deces YEAR  year of death if the tree does not give it (alias: --death-year)
  --tous        also show the following orders (default: the applicable order only) (alias: --all)
  --md file     write the table as Markdown (sensitive document: contains living people)

WHAT THE TOOL DOES: finds in the tree the possible heirs by order (descendants; father, mother,
siblings; ordinary ascendants; ordinary collaterals up to the 6th degree), applies representation
and the split between lines (fente), and says for each what must be proved.
WHAT THE TOOL DOES NOT DO: it does not replace a notary or a professional heir researcher. It ignores the
spouse's rights, wills, gifts, renunciation, unworthiness, adoption and foreign law. The shares shown are
indicative; the applicable order depends on the proof that an heir was alive at the death.
A "presumed alive" status is not proof: the birth record with its remarks is needed.
dev.st.same_year: died the same year ({dy}): establish the order of deaths
dev.st.alive: alive at the death (died {dy}: the share passes to his or her own heirs)
dev.st.presumed_alive: born {by}, no death known: to be proved alive
dev.share.tbd: to be set with a notary
dev.link.self: in his or her own right
dev.noyear: Year of death unknown: give it with --deces YEAR.
dev.title: # Indicative legal devolution (French law): {person}
dev.assumptions: Year of death used: **{year}**. Assumptions: French law, no will or gift, no renunciation, no adoption; the spouse's rights are not calculated. To be validated by a notary.
dev.spouses: **Spouse(s) in the tree**: {names}. Check that the marriage was not dissolved at the death; the spouse's rights depend on the other heirs (art. 756 ff.) and are not calculated here.
dev.order2: 2nd order: father, mother, siblings and their descendants (art. 734, 736, 738, 751)
dev.order3: 3rd order: ordinary ascendants, split in halves between the two lines (art. 734, 746)
dev.order4: 4th order: ordinary collaterals up to the 6th degree, the nearest in each line (art. 734, 753, 755)
dev.applicable: ← **applicable order** if the heirs are proved alive
dev.none_heirs: No possible heir in the tree.
dev.table.head: | Heir | Link | Status at the date of death | Indicative share | To prove |
dev.table.row: | {label} | {link} | {status} | {share} | birth record (parentage, remarks) of the heir and of each link up to the deceased; death records of those who died earlier; proof that he or she is alive |
dev.noheir: **No heir found up to the 6th degree in this tree.** Either the tree is incomplete or the estate is unclaimed; consult a notary (vacant estate, curator).
dev.next.title: ## Next steps
dev.next.1: 1. Prove each link with a record (level A): see `references/recherche-heritiers.md`.
dev.next.2: 2. Prove that each heir is alive or dead (marginal remarks, death register since 1970).
dev.next.3: 3. Complete the tree with missing branches (half-siblings, children born out of wedlock, adoptions).
dev.next.4: 4. Go through the notary in charge of the estate for contacts, the devolution and the certificate of heirship.
dev.written: (written to {path}: sensitive document, keep it local)
rep.help:
Report of proofs and open questions, as PDF (or dependency-free HTML).

Usage: python rapport_preuves.py <db> <output.pdf> [--titre "..."] [--tout] [--html]
       (aliases: --title, --everything)

Content: proofs (level A), uncertain facts (C and doubtful), leads not yet proved (research
log), open questions (help requested, inconsistencies), legend of the levels.

Privacy: by default, people who are probably alive are excluded from the document: born less than
100 years ago with no recorded death, or with no date at all but a parent, child or spouse of such a person. Every line
(proof, log, question, inconsistency) that names one of these people, in any form (case,
accents, order of first and last name), is removed and only counted. The hiding is deliberately cautious: a
historical namesake may be removed too. `--tout` turns the hiding off
(keep that document local). PDF: `reportlab` library (pip install reportlab); without it, or with
`--html`, the script writes an HTML page that can be printed to PDF from a browser.
rep.default_title: Report of proofs and open questions
rep.level.B: notice, tree or transcription: no record seen
rep.sec.legend: Legend of the levels of certainty
rep.sec.proofs: Proofs: facts established by a record (level A)
rep.sec.leads: Leads found, not yet proved (research log)
rep.sec.questions: Open questions ({n} request(s) for help pending)
rep.col.question: Question or request for help
rep.anom.intro: Inconsistencies found in the tree, to check in the records:
rep.pdf.intro: {date} · {n} people in the database · proofs by level: {levels}
rep.footer: {title} · generated on {date} · personal data, keep it local
rep.no_reportlab: reportlab missing: `pip install reportlab`, or run again with --html (page to print as PDF).
imp.help:
Import a GEDCOM file (Geneanet, Heredis, ... export) into the investigation database.

Usage: python gedcom_import.py tree.ged investigation.db [--label "Family X tree, export of 2026-11-02"]
Standard library only. People, events (birth, death, marriage, etc.) and
relations (spouse, parent) are created; every event is attached to a source
"GEDCOM import" of level B (transcription of a tree, not a record seen).
imp.done: Imported: {persons} people, {events} events, {rels} relations from {file} (source no. {source}, level B).
exp.help:
Export the investigation database as GEDCOM 5.5.1 (UTF-8), importable into Geneanet, Heredis, Ancestris.

Usage: python gedcom_export.py investigation.db tree_out.ged
Standard library only. Exports people, events and relations (spouse, parent).
The A/B/C levels of certainty stay in the database; the GEDCOM does not carry them.
gen.help:
Single entry point of the genealogy tools (Python 3.8 or later, no mandatory dependency).

Usage: python genealogie.py [--lang fr|en|de] <command> [arguments]

  init      <db>                            create the investigation database
  importer  <tree.ged> <db> [--label]       load a GEDCOM (level B)            (alias: import)
  exporter  <db> <tree.ged>                 write a GEDCOM                     (alias: export)
  analyse   <db> <cmd> [options]            stats, tache, frontiere, anomalies, manquants,
                                            correlations, parente A B, trouver PATTERN   (alias: analyze)
  valider   <db> [--racine X] [--lecteur "First name"]   local validation interface        (alias: validate)
  rapport   <db> <output.pdf> [--tout|--html|--titre "..."]   report of proofs and questions   (alias: report)
  devolution <db> <deceased> [--deces YEAR] [--tous] [--md f.md]   possible heirs by order (France)   (alias: inheritance)

Language: --lang fr|en|de, or the GENEALOGIE_LANG variable, or the system language (French by default).
Command and option names keep their French identifiers; English aliases are accepted
(import, export, analyze, validate, report, inheritance; --root, --reader, --death-year, --all, --title).
`python genealogie.py <command> --help` shows the help of that tool.
ui.help:
Local interface to validate proofs (in the browser, on this machine only).

Usage: python validation_ui.py <db> [--racine "Name or no."] [--port 8765] [--lecteur "First name"]
       (aliases: --root, --reader)

One card per person: birth, marriage, death, with the current level of certainty.
For each fact, one click: A (record read), B (notice, no record), C (deduction), ? (doubtful).
Optional field "reference / where read". Cards go from the ancestors closest to the root
to the most distant. Results are written to the `evidence` table of the database.

Security: the server only listens on 127.0.0.1 and requires a random token (shown at launch).
Data never leaves the machine. Standard library only.

(Ctrl+C to stop; the data stays on this machine.)
